title: Contain ordinary POSIX descendants of shared Git blob readers
body:
A Git blob response deadline can expire while the read stays blocked: the direct Git process exits, but an ordinary descendant still holds stdout. The shared reader now owns a POSIX session and stops that process group on timeout, success, malformed response or early generator close. Watchdog and finalizer share one idempotent stop operation; consumer pauses remain outside the response deadline.

The implementation preserves one-blob streaming, exact bytes, the first-request/no-response/exit129 NUL fallback gate and strict source authority. All actual consumers use the same reader: source validation, sparse manifest discovery, scaffold generation, committed-byte checking and export. Frozen packages and their pins are unchanged; this does not resolve their existing historical source-drift failures.

Validation on CPython 3.12.7/macOS arm64:

- 57 shared Git tests pass normal and optimized with warnings as errors. Six new real-process methods cover four stalled boundaries, leader exit, success/error cleanup, early close, consumer suspension and legacy fallback. Child readiness and stopped state are checked before teardown. A direct-child-only mutant still hangs with its child alive.
- 35 actual caller tests pass in each mode: scaffold, committed bytes, sparse planning and export.
- A fresh committed source snapshot with no Git directory and only the ps observer on PATH passes all six new tests normal/optimized, with source bytes unchanged.

The earlier optimized sandbox attempt denied the ps observer; final runs with process-observation permission pass. No scientific or historical full-suite replay was run. The ownership contract covers ordinary POSIX descendants remaining in the group with retained signal permissions; escaped sessions, abrupt outer-process death, Windows descendant ownership and separate Git-command deadlines remain outside scope. Native Linux/Windows and hosted CI are not claimed. The documentation records source attribution and open obligations.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4681#discussioncomment-19144823
Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; original attribution and Apache-2.0 retained.

Hosted CI caveat: the `research/a5-conjugate-any-registers` replay failed in [job120404022675](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39950023707/job/120404022675) for PR head `7a9d3b2d12cef85374145c315e14220342a4400e` (GitHub tested its merge with `ec2780e8`). Its unchanged package-local source checker rejects `certificates/selected-result.json`: pinned SHA256 `bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129`, actual `6fe0a099b89aa2aed796a13c3a21dafc63f3388ebf397464e44e0451893b9375`. Actual bytes are identical at this PR’s base and head; the hosted target base has the same hash. The frozen checker hashes provenance rows against live files, whereas generic metadata/pin validation authenticates their historical source pins. Targeted source-only reproduction gives the identical rejection; metadata/pins pass. The catalogue provenance pin is also already stale. No frozen artifact or pin was changed, and this is not a claim that all hosted checks pass or that the historical scientific replay succeeded.
